nodes.label: Fixture: Reverse-Chronological Company-Block Resume
nodes.rationale: Company name on its own line followed by title, date range, then a paragraph of prose bullets; skills appear in a trailing untitled 'MORE' list. Reverse-chronological order with no inline skill section and two degrees, testing role/company association when the order is inverted and skills are not adjacent to the experience.

nodes.label: Fixture: Canonical Section-Header Resume
nodes.rationale: Well-formed ATS-style resume: uppercase section headers (PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY, TECHNICAL SKILLS, WORK EXPERIENCE, EDUCATION, PROJECTS, CERTIFICATIONS), pipe-delimited contact line, 'Title | Company | Mon YYYY - Mon YYYY' job lines. Serves as the control case against which messier layouts are measured.

nodes.label: Fixture: Informal Conversational Resume
nodes.rationale: Free-form lowercase chat-style resume: no section headers, no contact section, hedged claims ('react (kind of)', 'i think i used it?', '2020 or 2019 i forget exactly'), and an unquantified job description. Probes robustness of the LLM path and hallucination risk when evidence is ambiguous.

nodes.label: Fixture: Minimal Sparse Resume
nodes.rationale: Eight-line resume: name, email, one skill, one internship, one degree, no projects. Verifies the parser does not fabricate absent sections and that empty arrays and empty description strings round-trip through resume_data.

nodes.label: Fixture: Date-Leading Tabular Resume
nodes.rationale: Date-first employment rows ('2021–Present | Title @ Company') with ·-delimited skill lists and em-dashes in the header line. Inverts the canonical 'Title | Company | Dates' order, so it tests date-range detection and ordering inversion rather than mere text splitting.

nodes.label: En-Dash Mojibake in Parsed Duration Fields
nodes.norm_label: en-dash mojibake in parsed duration fields
nodes.rationale: En dashes in resume date ranges are stored as UTF-8 bytes decoded as latin-1/mojibake ('â€“' instead of '–') in five of the duration values across the tabular and chronological outputs. Implies the text-extraction path re-encodes bytes rather than decoding, so any downstream date parsing on duration will fail.
nodes.source_location: resume_tabular.txt and resume_chronological.txt PARSED JSON duration fields

nodes.label: Regex Skill Extractor False Positives and Unstated Skills
nodes.norm_label: regex skill extractor false positives and unstated skills
nodes.rationale: The regex skill pass over-extracts: it emits 'java' as a substring of JavaScript and 'express' from Express.js. In the messy parse it also emits 'go', 'java' and 'machine learning', which do not appear in the raw resume at all, so skill inventory is not confined to the source document. Directly bears on the merged-skills transparency decision and on parsing quality metrics.
nodes.source_location: skills arrays of resume_clean.txt and resume_messy.txt PARSED JSON

nodes.label: Fixture: Oversized Resume File (11.5 MB)
nodes.rationale: A ~11.5 MB PDF whose bytes are almost entirely 'x' padding after the %PDF-1.4 header — it declares no objects, no page tree and no text streams. It is a payload-size fixture, not a parseable document: it exercises upload rejection/limits on the PDF path and guarantees any parser invoked on it has nothing to extract.
nodes.source_location: whole file (binary padding, no page tree or text objects)

nodes.label: Parsed Output: resume_chronological.txt (Carol Martinez)
nodes.rationale: Company-block layout with an untitled 'MORE' skills list, reverse-chronological experience, and two degrees. The LLM synthesized a project entry from the Kafka event-streaming bullet and a second from the FastAPI order-processing bullet. Duration strings again contain mojibake ('March 2021 â€“ June 2025').

nodes.label: Parsed Output: resume_clean.txt (Jane Smith)
nodes.rationale: Canonical-format control case. 25 regex skills, 3 experience entries (Google, Meta, Startup Inc), 1 education entry (Stanford), 2 project groups (Open Source Contributions, Personal Projects). Skills include 'java', 'express', 'node.js' and 'ci/cd' which are substring artifacts of JavaScript, Express.js, Node.js and CI/CD in the raw text.

nodes.label: Parsed Output: resume_messy.txt (Bob Jones)
nodes.rationale: Informal free-text stress case. The LLM faithfully preserved vague titles ('software engineer thing', 'did some stuff with backend') and hallucinated the graduation year as 2020 where the raw text says '2020 or 2019 i forget exactly'. The regex skills list nonetheless includes 'java', 'go', 'machine learning' and 'mysql' — terms absent from the raw text.

nodes.label: Parsed Output: resume_minimal.txt (John Doe)
nodes.rationale: Sparsity case. Single skill (python), one experience entry with an empty description string, one education entry, and an empty projects array — the no-data shape of the resume_data contract.

nodes.label: Parsed Output: resume_tabular.txt (Alice Chen)
nodes.rationale: Date-leading, delimiter-separated (· and |) layout with an em-dash in the title line. The LLM inverted the date-first employment rows into the correct title/company/duration shape, but duration strings came back with mojibake ('2021â€“Present').

nodes.label: Manual Conflict Resolution Surfaced in UI
nodes.norm_label: manual conflict resolution surfaced in ui
nodes.rationale: Conflicts between data sources are surfaced to the user for manual resolution rather than auto-resolved, per architecture.md §4 'surface conflicts transparently rather than resolving them silently'. Trade-off: users must manually review conflicts — chosen to give users control.

nodes.label: Merged Skills View with Source and Confidence Labels
nodes.norm_label: merged skills view with source and confidence labels
nodes.rationale: All skills from all sources are shown with source and confidence labels for transparency so users can see where each skill came from. Known impact: duplicate skills may appear with different sources (e.g. 'Python (github)' and 'Python (resume)'). Spec reference: architecture.md §4 'compute the merged view as a derived field'.

nodes.label: MinIO as Default S3-Compatible Storage Backend
nodes.norm_label: minio as default s3-compatible storage backend
nodes.rationale: Local MinIO chosen as the default because it is easier for local development; production will use AWS S3 or Cloudflare R2. Impact: none — the choice is configuration-driven via environment variables. Spec reference: architecture.md §2 'S3-compatible bucket'.

nodes.label: Regex-Only Resume Parsing (v1 decision)
nodes.rationale: Regex/keyword extraction chosen over LLM-enhanced parsing for v1 because LLM calls cost money and add latency; regex works for standard resume formats and can be enhanced later. Impact: may miss complex formatting or non-standard layouts — acceptable for v1 MVP. Spec reference: architecture.md §5.3 mentions 'regex/keyword pass + LLM inference' — implemented regex only.

nodes.label: Profile Snapshot Update-In-Place (No New Versions)
nodes.rationale: Existing snapshot rows are updated rather than versioned, chosen for simplicity in v1; the architecture still allows versioning later. Impact: previous snapshot data is overwritten — acceptable for v1. Spec reference: architecture.md §3.3 shows a single profile_snapshots table with no versioning.

nodes.label: Hybrid Extraction: Regex Skills + LLM Experience/Education/Projects
nodes.norm_label: hybrid extraction: regex skills + llm experience/education/projects
nodes.rationale: The live Phase 1 pipeline splits work by field: skills are regex-extracted while experience, education, and projects are LLM-extracted via openai/gpt-4o-mini through backend/services/resume_ai.py, with the result written to profile_snapshots.resume_data. Generated for human review before Phase 1 sign-off.
